body:
In the early 600s, a new religion, Islam, began in the Arabian Peninsula. Within about a hundred years, Muslim rulers governed lands from Spain to Central Asia. Arabic became a shared language of government, trade and learning across that huge area.

By 800 CE, the city of Baghdad was one of the largest in the world. Scholars there translated books from Greek, Persian and Indian languages into Arabic, and they added new ideas of their own in mathematics, medicine and astronomy. Words such as algebra and algorithm come from this time.

In this unit you will:
- explain how Islam and the Arabic language spread,
- analyze a scholar's own words about why he wrote a mathematics book,
- trace one idea that traveled from the Islamic world to other places.

Key words: Islam, Quran, caliph, caliphate, hajj, Abbasid, translation, scholar.

Question to keep in mind: why do some cities become centers of learning?
title: Crossroads of Faith, Trade and Learning
